lines: In these generated files gitleaks matches only rules that take any string of high entropy, which hashes and minified names are as well, or the curl lines a page of built documentation copies from its source, so the matches are not reported as secrets:
vendor/alipaysdk/easysdk/csharp/UnitTest/Util/AES/ClientTest.cs, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
vendor/alipaysdk/easysdk/csharp/UnitTest/Util/Generic/ClientTest.cs, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
vendor/alipaysdk/easysdk/java/src/test/java/com/alipay/easysdk/TestAccount.java, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
vendor/alipaysdk/easysdk/java/src/test/java/com/alipay/easysdk/util/aes/ClientTest.java, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
vendor/alipaysdk/easysdk/java/src/test/java/com/alipay/easysdk/util/generic/ClientTest.java, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
vendor/alipaysdk/easysdk/php/test/util/generic/ClientTest.php, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
A key a build takes from the environment ends up in such a file too: where one of them has no reason to carry a key, look at it.
